newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel plans global tender for land gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Israel plans global tender for land gas pipeline.

text.p: Israel's infrastructure ministry said on Wednesday it would issue an international tender to build and operate an overland pipeline to supply about 30 percent of Israel's natural gas market.

The concession is an adjunct to a proposed undersea pipeline between Egypt and Israel to supply gas to state-owned Israel Electric Corp, the electrical utility that is expected to consume 70 percent of future Israeli demand for natural gas.

"The gas company that will be chosen by international tender will receive a limited-period concession to lay the gas pipeline inside of Israel, to operate it, and to purchase and market gas for customers other than the Electric Corporation," the ministry said in a statement.
The ministry said the tender would place emphasis on the speed to introduce gas into the Israeli economy and on transport costs.
Israel has been trying to reach long-term agreements on gas sales to diversify its energy sources and lower energy costs.
The undersea pipeline would run under the Mediterranean Sea to three coastal Israeli power plants.

Israel Electric Corp is expected to begin talks in the next few weeks with Amoco and Agip SpA to import Egyptian natural gas. Both companies are jointly developing a gas field in Egypt's Nile delta. Those talks are aimed at bypassing negotiations between the Israeli and Egyptian governments, industry sources said.
The Infrastructure Ministry said it was laying the groundwork for legislation on a natural gas law and on rights of passage on land and sea.
